shots.action: a huge wave crashing over the tiny hatchling, tumbling her backwards, then she flips and swims

shots.action: the hatchling swimming alone through the vast blue ocean, a big fish shadow passing below
shots.camera: epic wide shot, slow pull-back

shots.action: a huge adult loggerhead turtle hauling herself up the same moonlit beach to nest
shots.camera: close-up, slow push-in, then hold

episodes.description:
Neutrophils are white blood cells that rush to infections, squeeze through vessel walls, eat bacteria, and can burst to release sticky DNA nets (NETs) that trap germs. Pus is largely made of dead neutrophils.

shots.action: a glowing DNA web full of trapped bacteria as more white cells arrive
shots.camera: epic wide shot, slow pull-back
shots.narration: The net traps the invaders. More of her sisters arrive and do the same. Wave after wave, they give everything.

shots.action: the cut healing from the inside, new skin closing over in warm light
shots.camera: close-up, slow push-in, then hold
shots.narration: That yellow stuff in an infected cut? That's mostly them. Tiny soldiers who died for you.
